reviews.title: Helpful tool to quit
reviews.text: I’m coming up on 3 years smoke free next month. I quit cold turkey after about 2 years of preparation. It’s possible and, for me, after the first year, I can honestly say I rarely think about it. Smoked for 32 years. I still keep the widget and a couple of times a year check it to see how much money I’ve not spent, over 12k at this point. You can do it. You can do hard things.

If you want to quite I know you can! Best of luck everyone!!

reviews.title: Perfect for ADHD brain
reviews.text: Honestly, I’ve tried to quit smoking for a while now. Using this app has gotten me further than any other attempts. The reward system and information is so helpful for my adhd brain. It made it a fun challenge to quit smoking without the guilt and shame. The daily totals are my favorite and it really puts it into perspective how much time and money I’ve wasted over the past 14 years I’ve been smoking. I LOVE this app. And my children have been begging me to quit smoking for years, so as much as I hate that it’s become a family activity to check this app obsessively, it has! And it’s never felt better to try to quit a habit I actually kind of loved.

reviews.title: Helps but they could add some features.
reviews.text: This app plus nicotine gum really helped me quit smoking but if you break your streak and start again the only way to save your progress is by screenshotting a picture of it. If i make it 154 days and then smoke for 2 weeks and start again there should be something that holds that 154 days in its memory. It should just restart your progress because you have in fact made progress.
